facts.t: Non-citizens can bring environmental cases before the NGT
facts.d: Betty C. Alvares v. State of Goa settled it — environmental justice does not turn on nationality. Very few Indian forums are open on those terms.

facts.t: The NGT cannot hear Wildlife Protection Act cases
facts.d: Its jurisdiction excludes both the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act, 2006. A tribunal built for environmental adjudication is barred from two of the most consequential environmental statutes.

facts.t: India was the third country in the world to create one
facts.d: After Australia and New Zealand, India became the third nation with a dedicated environmental court, and the first developing country to do so — under the NGT Act, 2010.

bank.q: The National Green Tribunal was established under an Act of:
bank.e: The NGT Act, 2010, making India the third country in the world with a dedicated environmental court.

bank.q: With reference to the NGT's jurisdiction, consider the following statements:
s: It excludes the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
It excludes the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
Only Indian citizens may approach it.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Betty C. Alvares held that non-citizens may file environmental cases before it.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (principle applied):
pairs: A. Srinagar Bandh Aapda Sangharsh Samiti
1. Polluter pays, applied to marine pollution
2. No fault liability for power companies
3. Suspension of clearance to protect endangered species
4. Implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules
bank.e: No fault liability, polluter pays, solid waste rules and species protection respectively.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the NGT's recognised achievements?
o: Banning old diesel vehicles in Delhi
Framing the Environment Protection Act's parent rules
bank.e: Rule-making under the Environment (Protection) Act belongs to the executive, not to the tribunal.

bank.as: The NGT has been criticised for weak enforcement.
bank.rs: Many of its orders remain unimplemented, and it relies substantially on self-assessment reports from the entities it regulates.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — a tribunal that can order but cannot compel.

bank.q: Consider the following criticisms of the NGT:
s: Chronic understaffing leaves benches below mandated strength.
Delegation to expert committees can bypass hearings and violate natural justice.
Its suo motu powers were struck down as beyond the statutory mandate.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Ankita Sinha (2021) upheld the NGT's suo motu powers, though allegations of overreach persist.

bank.q: Almitra H. Patel v. UoI concerned the implementation of:
bank.e: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, along with a prohibition on open burning of waste.

bank.q: All of the following are stated rationales for creating the NGT EXCEPT:
o: Replacing High Court jurisdiction over environmental matters
A less formal and less expensive forum
bank.e: High Court jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 survives — L. Chandra Kumar makes its exclusion constitutionally impossible.

bank.q: Which recent NGT direction concerned pan-India guidelines?
o: Silica mining, directed to the CPCB
bank.e: The tribunal directed the Central Pollution Control Board to frame pan-India silica mining guidelines.

bank.q: With reference to proposed reforms, consider the following:
s: Expanding jurisdiction to include all relevant environmental laws.
Removing the requirement to hear all parties in order to speed up disposal.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are proposed. The reform on hearings runs the other way — ensuring all parties are heard and preventing undue delegation.
